questions.question: Which sequence follows air from the upper airway into progressively smaller lower-airway structures?

choices.text: Pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles
Pharynx → trachea → larynx → bronchioles → bronchi
Larynx → pharynx → bronchi → trachea → bronchioles
Pharynx → larynx → bronchioles → bronchi → trachea

questions.explanation: The larynx leads into the trachea, which branches into bronchi and then bronchioles.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: This reverses both larynx/trachea and bronchi/bronchioles.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The pharynx precedes the larynx, and the trachea precedes the bronchi.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: The trachea is upstream of the bronchial branches.

questions.question: During normal spontaneous inhalation, which sequence draws air into the lungs?

choices.text: Diaphragm contracts → thoracic volume increases → intrathoracic pressure falls
Diaphragm relaxes → thoracic volume increases → intrathoracic pressure rises
Diaphragm contracts → thoracic volume decreases → intrathoracic pressure rises
Diaphragm relaxes → thoracic volume decreases → intrathoracic pressure falls

questions.explanation: Contraction enlarges the chest and produces negative pressure that draws air inward.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Relaxation normally reduces thoracic volume; rising pressure does not draw air in.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Contraction increases rather than decreases thoracic volume.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Decreasing volume increases pressure and supports exhalation.

questions.question: Which event is external respiration?

Oxygen crosses from systemic capillaries into muscle cells
Oxygen binds to hemoglobin for transport

Greater surface tension and a tendency for bronchi to dilate

Reduced pulmonary blood flow with unchanged alveolar stability

questions.question: A rise in blood carbon dioxide with a fall in pH normally produces which response?

choices.text: Chemoreceptor signaling increases respiratory rate and depth
Chemoreceptor signaling suppresses breathing until oxygen falls
The diaphragm relaxes continuously to increase air entry

incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Continuous relaxation would not produce effective inhalation.

questions.question: Air reaches an alveolar region, but a pulmonary vascular obstruction prevents blood from reaching it. Why can oxygen delivery still fail?

choices.text: Ventilation without matching perfusion cannot transfer that oxygen into circulating blood
The region has inadequate ventilation, but preserved perfusion
The region has adequate ventilation and perfusion, but impaired systemic metabolism
The region has increased oxygen transfer because pulmonary flow is reduced

questions.explanation: Effective exchange requires air and blood to reach the same alveolar region.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: The stem specifies that air arrives but blood does not; the deficit is perfusion.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Perfusion of the specified alveolar region is impaired.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Reduced pulmonary flow limits gas transfer rather than increasing it.

questions.question: Which set of findings most strongly supports adequate breathing in an adult?

choices.text: Regular 16/min respirations, sufficient depth, equal chest rise, and clear bilateral sounds
Regular 16/min respirations, minimal depth, and barely detectable air movement
24/min respirations with retractions and unequal chest expansion
10/min respirations with irregular pauses and increasing drowsiness

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: A normal rate does not compensate for low tidal volume.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Retractions and unequal movement indicate abnormal breathing.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Slow irregular breathing and declining alertness suggest inadequate ventilation.

Treat the displayed number as the sole determinant of oxygen and ventilation needs
Use the unstable reading to confirm carbon monoxide poisoning

questions.question: A low end-tidal CO2 value is obtained in a patient with shock. Which interpretation is most defensible?

choices.text: Reduced pulmonary blood flow may lower CO2 delivery to the lungs; low ETCO2 does not prove hyperventilation
Reduced pulmonary blood flow raises ETCO2, so this value establishes hyperventilation
Low ETCO2 indicates carbon dioxide retention from hypoventilation
Low ETCO2 rules out impaired perfusion when spontaneous breathing is present

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Reduced delivery of CO2 to the lungs can lower rather than raise the measured value.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Carbon dioxide retention is associated with high rather than low ETCO2 in the stated interpretation.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Spontaneous breathing does not exclude reduced pulmonary perfusion.

questions.question: In an unresponsive nontrauma patient, an otherwise well-sealed ventilation mask produces little chest rise. Snoring is still heard. What is the best initial correction?

Increase oxygen flow without changing airway position
Squeeze the bag faster to overcome the snoring

incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Reassess and correct technique rather than abandoning ventilation.
